findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class that cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data. Instantiating the handler therefore raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of type metric_alert_fire will crash in process_detectors. Previously the class had a concrete (stub) evaluate and worked. Either implement the hooks or keep it as a plain DetectorHandler stub.

findings.title: New abstract method breaks existing StatefulDetectorHandler subclasses
findings.body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is added as an abstractmethod, so every existing subclass must implement it or fail at instantiation. This is the cause of the MetricAlertDetectorHandler breakage. A non-abstract default, or a documented contract, would be safer.

findings.title: Exception from hook could skip commit of state updates
findings.body: Occurrences are produced inside the loop before commit_state_updates. If build_occurrence_and_event_data or produce_occurrence_to_kafka raises, dedupe and state updates for that detector are never committed. The packet is then reprocessed and occurrences can be emitted twice. Conversely, state is committed after the produce calls, so a commit failure after a successful produce leaves the same duplicate risk.
